data.text:
Handoff from the planning session (2026-09-14). Read in this order before touching code:

1. project/2026-09-14-architecture-plan.md — Decisions and Invariants are binding; each leaf names its files.
2. project/2026-09-14-research-findings.md — the verified wire facts. Sections 1 (Anthropic), 2 (OpenRouter) and 3 (Go 1.27) are what the provider and foundation leaves implement; do not re-research them, and do not trust prior training on json/v2 tag names (`embed`, not `inline`; no `format` or `unknown` options).
3. project/gotchas.md and project/backlog.md.

Things that are true but easy to get wrong:

- Go builds and git both fail inside the Bash sandbox ("package fmt is not in std", unreadable ~/.gitconfig); re-run that one call with the sandbox off. File edits and `job` work sandboxed.
- json/v2 marshaler funcs may receive *T rather than T for union members; handle both.
- Property order in tool schemas is load-bearing: never a map anywhere a schema lives.
- On OpenRouter the trailing usage frame repeats finish_reason; on both providers a 200 can carry an error body.
- Thinking blocks are opaque: keep the provider's raw block and re-emit it byte-exact and in order. Never edit an earlier turn.
- The `claude-api` skill will tell you to use anthropic-sdk-go; the core takes no dependencies. Use the skill for facts only.
- API keys will be in .env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY) when the fixture leaves are reached; the unit suite must pass without them.

Suggested first moves: `job orient` points at the scaffold leaf (fzGDQ2). The foundation leaves after it (blocks, schema, vocab, sse, markdown) are disjoint by file and can fan out to parallel agents once the scaffold lands; tools and stream depend on them. Both providers can then run in parallel. Verification scratch from planning (a json/v2 and generic-method probe) is disposable and lives only in the session scratchpad.

Implemented internal/sse (sse.go, sse_test.go, split_test.go) per the architecture plan's SSE leaf and the WHATWG event-stream spec.

TDD: wrote sse_test.go and split_test.go first, referencing Event/Events/eventsWithLimit/splitSSELines before any implementation existed; `go test ./internal/sse/...` failed to compile (undefined: Event, Events, splitSSELines, ...) confirming red. One gotcha hit while writing tests: a Go string literal containing an actual BOM character (`"﻿"`) makes the compiler reject the *source file itself* with "illegal byte order mark" — Go disallows a literal BOM anywhere in source except as the very first bytes. Fixed by using the byte escape `"\xEF\xBB\xBF"` instead, which is plain ASCII in the source and only becomes the BOM bytes at runtime. Documented this in project/gotchas.md.

Design:
- Event{Type, Data, ID, Retry} as decided. Events(io.Reader) iter.Seq2[Event, error]: a pure pull iterator, no goroutine, so an early `break` by the consumer just stops calling Read — proved with a byte-counting reader.
- Custom bufio.SplitFunc (splitSSELines) handles LF/CRLF/lone-CR, including a CR at the very end of a buffered chunk (asks bufio.Scanner for more data unless atEOF, so a CRLF pair split across reads is never mis-split — proved with iotest.OneByteReader end-to-end and with direct two-call unit tests).
- BOM stripped via bufio.Reader.Peek(3)/Discard before the Scanner is attached.
- Buffer capped at 64 MiB via scanner.Buffer(initial, max), with initial = min(4096, max) so a test can inject a tiny max (64 bytes) and prove an oversized line yields bufio.ErrTooLong rather than being silently dropped, without allocating a real 64 MiB line in the test.
- Two decided deviations from the literal WHATWG algorithm, both documented on Events' doc comment:
  1. (given in the brief) event: arriving while data is pending dispatches the pending event first, as if a blank line preceded it.
  2. (my own consistent extension, not explicit in the brief) ID and Retry do NOT carry forward across dispatches the way the spec's "last event id buffer" does — every Event reflects only the fields its own group set. The brief explicitly decided this for ID ("keep the API simple: ID is what this event set") but was silent on Retry; I applied the same rule to Retry for consistency, since the alternative (Retry persisting silently across events, ID not) would be an inconsistent, surprising API. Flagging this explicitly since it's an extrapolation, not a literal instruction.
- Event.Type defaults to "message" when no event: field was ever sent for that dispatch, per spec (https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#dispatchMessage). The brief's DECIDED API section didn't state this default explicitly; implemented it because omitting it would make every default-typed OpenRouter/Anthropic-shaped test data line come back with Type == "", which no consumer would want.

Verified before handback (worktree, sandbox disabled): go fix ./..., gofmt -l . (empty), go vet ./..., go mod tidy (no-op, confirms zero deps), go build ./..., go test -race ./... — all green, whole module. internal/sse/sse.go is 237 lines, sse_test.go 286, split_test.go 73 — all comfortably under the 400-line ceiling.

data.text:
Vocabulary landed on wt/vocab (worktree .claude/worktrees/vocab), not committed.

Files: stop_reason.go, thinking.go, usage.go, decimal.go, capabilities.go, errors.go plus a test file for each. `go fix ./...`, `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...` clean; `go test -race ./...` passes (38 tests, all red first).

Three judgement calls the next reader should know:

1. **Decimal is a canonical decimal string, not a *big.Int + scale.** Arithmetic converts to math/big on demand and canonicalises the result ("" is zero, no exponent, no trailing zeros), so two Decimals holding the same number are always `==`. A `*big.Int` field would have made `Cost == Cost` and `Pricing == Pricing` compare pointers silently, and a `big.Int` value field would have made those structs uncomparable and unsafe to copy. Prices are parsed once and added a few thousand times per run, so re-parsing per op costs nothing that matters. Untrusted input is bounded: at most 4096 significant digits and |scale| <= 4096, so "1e2000000000" is an error rather than a 2 GB allocation.

2. **Cost.Add treats the zero Cost as the identity, then ANDs Reported.** Strict AND alone makes the natural accumulator (`var total Cost; total = total.Add(c)`) report false forever, because the empty accumulator is unreported. Anthropic's "no cost reported" *is* the zero Cost, so it contributes nothing and clears nothing; a non-identity leg that was not reported still poisons the total, because a sum that omits a leg must not present itself as a provider's figure. Costs in different currencies are summed but marked not reported.

3. **StopReason gained `StopNone = ""`** (the brief listed only the six wire values) so the zero value has a name and `Known()` can be true for every constant the package defines. `Known()` is therefore an "is this one of ours" check, not an "is this set" check; ask `== StopNone` for the latter.

Also worth knowing downstream: `Capabilities` carries `ThinkingEfforts []Effort`, so `Capabilities` and `ModelInfo` are not comparable with `==` — tests compare field by field. `ErrorKind("")` normalises to `KindUnknown` in String, Retryable and `(*APIError).Is`, so an unmapped error still answers `errors.Is(err, KindUnknown)`.

data.text: Vocabulary implemented and verified on wt/vocab; handing back to the integrator to commit and close.

Block model implemented: block.go, source.go, block_json.go, message.go, conversation.go and four test files. Suite green: `go test -race ./...` in the wt/blocks worktree; `go fix`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go mod tidy` all clean.

## json/v2 facts verified on go1.27.0 (scratch probe, then the suite)

1. **A bare `[]Block` cannot be unmarshalled.** `json.Unmarshal(data, &[]Block{})` fails with "cannot derive concrete type for nil interface with finite type set": json/v2 needs an `UnmarshalFromFunc` option for a non-empty interface, and a plain slice type gives nowhere to attach one. So a block list is the named type `Blocks []Block`, whose `UnmarshalJSONFrom` installs the dispatch internally. `Message.Content` and `ToolResult.Content` are `Blocks`; since `Blocks` and `[]Block` are mutually assignable, callers write `UserMessage(Text{...})` and `[]Block` parameters accept it unchanged. Plain `json.Marshal`/`Unmarshal` on a Message, a Conversation, and on `Blocks`, all round-trip with no options. The plan is corrected in place.

2. **Marshalling needs no options at all.** Each block type carries a `MarshalJSONTo` that writes its own `"type"` tag first, so a block is self-describing wherever it appears rather than only inside a container that knows to tag it. The tag is spliced on by a generic `tagged[T]{Type; Body T json:",embed"}` over a method-less defined type (`type textBody Text`), which keeps one struct per concept — the body types share the real struct's fields and tags, they are not hand-written twins. `,embed` (json/v2's rename of `inline`) works on a generic field.

3. **`[]byte` encodes as base64 by default.** No option needed for `Source.Data`.

4. **A `jsontext.Value` does not survive arbitrary whitespace.** The encoder reformats on `WriteValue`: insignificant whitespace is stripped and string escapes are normalised (`é` becomes the literal, `\/` becomes `/`); `jsontext.PreserveRawStrings` does not change this on the marshal path. What *is* preserved: member order, every member, and numbers verbatim. Provider wire bytes are compact, so `Thinking.Raw` and `Unknown.Raw` are byte-identical in practice, and semantically identical always. `TestThinkingRawSurvivesNesting` pins member-order preservation with a deliberately out-of-order raw block.

5. **`Decoder.ReadValue` bytes must be cloned.** Verified by mutation: with the `bytes.Clone` removed, decoding 40 blocks through `json.UnmarshalRead` over a `iotest.OneByteReader` gives block 0 a `Raw` of `,#"type":"alpha2"...` — the decoder had refilled its buffer underneath. Decoding the same input from a `[]byte` shows nothing, because that path aliases the caller's slice. Any future code that keeps bytes from a decoder (the SSE/stream leaf will) needs the same clone, and needs a reader-based test to catch its absence.

## Design decisions

- **Unknown is the fallback for a missing or unrecognised type tag** (invariant 6: surface, never drop), and it re-marshals as its raw bytes, so a block goodall does not understand passes through storage and back to the provider. A *known* type whose body is malformed is a decode error naming the block type instead — the two failures are different and stay distinguishable.
- **`Conversation.Append` allocates an exact-capacity slice.** The test asserts `cap == len` after every append as well as forking twice from the same value at eight different lengths; the behavioural fork check alone is not enough, because a naive `append` only aliases once the growth policy has left headroom (it first bites at length 3).
- **Accessors deep-copy far enough to matter**: the message's `Content` slice and any nested `ToolResult.Content`. `jsontext.Value` bytes are shared, read-only — nothing in the library writes through them, and copying every raw thinking block on every `At` would be the expensive part of a long thread.
- `is_error` and `partial` are `omitzero`, so a plain result and a complete turn carry no noise. `ToolUse.Input` is `omitzero` too, which keeps a nil input round-tripping as nil rather than as the four bytes `null`.
- `Conversation{}` marshals as `[]` rather than `null`, so a persisted thread always has one shape.

## Deviations from the brief

- `Blocks` named type, and `Message.Content`/`ToolResult.Content` typed as it (finding 1 — the brief's shape cannot decode).
- Marshalling by method rather than by `MarshalToFunc` (finding 2; the brief left the mechanism to the implementer).
- `Unknown.Type` is `BlockType`, a string enum, not `string`; `BlockType` constants name the seven known tags.
- Added `SystemMessage`, since `RoleSystem` exists and the other two roles have constructors.

## Gaps for whoever picks this up

- Nothing here validates a block's contents — an `Image` with no source, a `ToolResult` whose content holds a `ToolUse`. That belongs with the request builder, which knows what a provider accepts.
- `Blocks` is the only decode entry point. If an event or thread type outside this package needs a bare `[]Block` field, it wants `Blocks` instead, or this package should export the unmarshalers.

Shape as built:
- `Schema` is a plain struct whose eight members emit in a fixed order (type, description, enum, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, format), unset ones omitted by `omitzero`. `json.Marshal` with no options produces provider-ready bytes.
- `Properties []Property` carries its own MarshalJSONTo/UnmarshalJSONFrom so it is a JSON object on the wire but an ordered slice in Go. `Property.Schema` is a **value**, not a pointer (the brief left the choice open) — it removes a whole class of nil checks from Validate.
- `AdditionalProperties` is a named string with Unset/Forbidden/Allowed and a bool on the wire, so "absent" and "false" are different values rather than one zero bool.
- A nil `Properties` emits no `properties` member; an **empty non-nil** one emits `"properties":{}`. Inference always produces the non-nil form, so a no-parameter tool gets the `{"type":"object","properties":{}}` shape Anthropic documents.
- Errors are a typed `*SchemaError{Path, Reason}` so the tools leaf can report the field path without scraping the message.

Inference was written against **measured** json/v2 behaviour, not the assumed rules; the verified facts are now recorded as a dated block quote in project/2026-09-14-research-findings.md §3. The four that changed the implementation:

1. `[N]byte` is base64 like `[]byte` (and refuses a JSON array on the way back), while a slice of a *named* byte type stays a JSON array. The test is "element type is exactly `byte`".
2. An embedded field of **unexported type** is still encoded by json/v2, both flattened and when given an explicit JSON name. A first cut skipped it on `IsExported()` and silently dropped the property.
3. The `,string` tag option makes a number a JSON **string** and json/v2 then rejects a bare number, so such a field must infer as `string`; on a bool or string field json/v2 errors, and so does inference.
4. `encoding.TextMarshaler` beats structural encoding (`netip.Addr`, `time.Time`), and `time.Duration` has *no* representation in json/v2 at all — a schema promising an integer there would produce input the handler could never decode, so it is an inference error.

Embedded flattening implements json/v2's real depth rule: depth-first in place, a shallower field shadows a deeper one of the same name and keeps its own position, and two fields at the same depth claiming one name is an error. Recursion detection is path-scoped, so a struct used twice on sibling branches is fine while a type that reaches itself is an error naming the path.

For the tools leaf: call `SchemaFor[In]()` then `(*Schema).Validate()`. Validate does the five structural checks plus "additionalProperties only on an object", and recurses into properties and items with a dotted path (`origin.x`, `tags[]`) in the message.

Two things deliberately NOT done, for the owner to rule on:
- `[]byte` infers as a bare `{"type":"string"}` with no hint that the value must be base64. Adding `"format":"byte"` (OpenAPI's convention, widely recognised by models) would cut a likely decode failure; the brief only specified a format for `time.Time`, so it was left alone.
- `Validate` does not require an array schema to carry `items`. Inference always supplies one, but a hand-built `{"type":"array"}` meaning "any array" is legal JSON Schema and is allowed through.

internal/transport built on wt/transport (worktree .claude/worktrees/transport). Four source files: transport.go (Client, Request, Do, build, errorFor, KindForStatus), retry.go (defaults, full-jitter backoff, ctx-aware wait, Retry-After and request-id header parsing), body.go (the ctx-bound response body), plus fakes_test.go / transport_test.go / retry_test.go / stream_test.go. `go test -race ./...` passes; `go fix`, `gofmt -l`, `go vet`, `go mod tidy` clean.

Shape as decided in the integrator note, with these findings worth carrying into the provider tasks:

1. `MaxRetries` cannot express "no retries" with a zero field, because zero is what an uninitialised struct carries and zero means "take the default of 2". A negative value is the opt-out, and the field doc says so. The alternative (a *int) was not worth the pointer.

2. The cancellation promise needed a watcher goroutine, not just a read guard. net/http closes the body on ctx cancel only because the real Transport tears the connection down; an injected RoundTripper (a recorder, a replayer, a test fake) has no connection, so "cancelling ctx closes the body" would have been a promise that held only over real sockets. `newContextBody` therefore parks one goroutine per streamed response on `select { ctx.Done(); stop }`, released by Close (idempotent via sync.Once). It is skipped entirely when ctx.Done() is nil — a context that can never be cancelled needs no watcher, and a goroutine parked on a nil channel is NOT durably blocked, which would stall a synctest bubble.

3. synctest note for whoever writes the provider stream tests: inside a bubble, derive contexts from context.Background() rather than from t.Context(). The bubble's root goroutine exit waits for every bubbled goroutine, so a watcher parked on a context that is only cancelled when the test function returns is a deadlock. `context.WithCancel(context.Background())` inside the bubble creates a Done channel that is unambiguously bubbled, and `defer cancel()` releases the watcher.

4. Retry-After and the delay interact in three ways, all tested: honoured exactly and jitter-free when present and within MaxRetryAfter (default 30s); the error returned unretried, with RetryAfter set, when it is longer than that (the caller decides whether to sleep 15 minutes); and ignored when it is zero, negative, unparseable or an HTTP-date already in the past, which falls back to jitter rather than to a number nobody sent.

5. KindForStatus returns KindUnknown for anything it cannot place, including a status below 400 — the brief's table only covered >= 400, and a 3xx that escapes the redirect follower should not be classified by guesswork.

6. The fallback Message is truncated at 1024 bytes (the body is read bounded at 1 MiB). The full body still travels on Raw when it is valid JSON, so nothing is lost and an error stays printable in a log line.

Mutation proofs run rather than asserted: dropping the watcher goroutine fails TestCancelMidBodyClosesBody, TestDoCancelMidBodyOverRealConnection and TestDoReturnsSuccessBodyOpen; ignoring Retry-After when choosing the delay fails the two Retry-After timing tests, TestRetryAfterAboveCapIsNotRetried and TestDoRetriesOverRealConnection; dropping the truncation fails TestDoFallbackTruncatesAHugeBody.

Nothing outside internal/transport was touched. deps_test.go's stdOnly list is unchanged and should stay that way: internal/transport imports the root package by design, so it does not belong in a std-only list.

DECISION — required parameters. Verified on go1.27.0 darwin/arm64 (scratch module, json.Unmarshal with RejectUnknownMembers): encoding/json/v2 does NOT enforce required members. `{}` decodes into a struct with no error, leaving every field at its zero value, so a model that omits `city` would silently run the tool on "". That breaks the promise the schema made to the model, so Execute checks the decoded object against the schema's Required list after a successful decode — recursively, through nested objects (`window.start`) and array elements (`points[1].lon`) — and returns the same IsError shape a decode failure returns: `missing required parameter "window.start"` (plural: `missing required parameters "query" and "window"`). An author happy with the zero value marks the field omitzero, which is exactly what makes it optional in the schema. Cost: one extra pass over the input as map[string]jsontext.Value per call. Recorded as a block quote under the plan's Tools paragraph.

DECISION — the error text. One problem line, a blank line, then the whole parameter listing in schema order:

    parameter "days" takes an integer, but the value sent was 3.5

    Parameters:
      city (string, required): the city to look up
      units (string, optional, one of "celsius", "fahrenheit"): temperature units
      days (integer, optional): how many days to forecast

Nested objects get dotted names, array elements a [] suffix (`points[].lat`), arrays their element type (`array of string`), time.Time-style fields their format. A tool with no parameters says "This tool takes no parameters." rather than an empty heading. Problem lines: `unknown parameter "window.stop"`, `parameter "x" takes …, but the value sent was …`, `the input must be a JSON object, but …`, `the input is not valid JSON: <jsontext inner error>`, `missing required parameter(s) …`.

FACT worth knowing downstream: json/v2 populates SemanticError.JSONValue only when it rejected a string's or number's *content* (3.5 into an int); a plain kind mismatch (string into int) carries JSONKind only. So the message names the literal when it has one and the JSON kind otherwise — it cannot always echo the value.

Also: an absent input (nil, empty, whitespace, `null`) is read as `{}`; `Schema()` returns the same *Schema pointer every call; result helpers leave ToolUseID empty; run's result and error pass through untouched; run is not called at all when the input fails to decode.

Mutation check done: reversing the property iteration in appendParameterLines made both listing-order assertions fail with the reversed text, then reverted.

Decisions the next leaves need:

1. **`UnknownEvent`, not `Unknown`.** The brief's event name collided with the `Unknown` *block* in the same package. It is `UnknownEvent{EventType EventType; Raw jsontext.Value}`, tagged `{"type":"unknown","event_type":"<provider tag>","raw":{...}}`. Unlike the unknown block it does NOT re-emit raw verbatim: an event goes to a front end and never back to a provider, so a front end's switch on `type` never meets a surprise value.

2. **`Event` has an exported `Type() EventType`** alongside the unexported seal, so the chat layer can route or log without a full type switch, and `EventType.FromLoop()` splits the loop's six from the provider's ten.

3. **Usage folding: later report wins field by field, zero means "not reported here".** Anthropic puts the input side on `message_start` and cumulative counts on `message_delta`; OpenRouter sends one trailing frame. Counts only grow within a message, so a zero in the later report is silence, not a reset, and the earlier figure stands. `laterUsage` in accumulate.go; three table cases in TestAccumulatorUsage.

4. **`Accumulator.Response()` is never nil**, at any point in the stream; `Message.Partial` is the single signal of completeness. `Collect` therefore always hands back a response, even alongside an error, so a cancelled stream still yields its text and its usage.

5. **An open tool call's `Input` is left empty in `Message()`/`snapshot()`.** Half a JSON document is not a JSON value and a `Message` holding one fails to marshal exactly when a UI wants to draw it. The fragments are on the `ToolInputDelta` events for anyone who wants them; at `BlockStop` an empty input becomes `{}` and an invalid one is a `*ProtocolError` (a truncated call must never run).

6. **`Prefix()` stops at the first still-open block** rather than returning every finished block, because a prefix is what can be replayed and a thinking signature binds everything after it.

7. **`ProtocolError` lives in stream.go** (with `Stream`, `Collect`, `CollectResult`), not accumulate.go, which was over the 400-line ceiling with it.

8. Providers: `ToolChoice.Validate()` is there to be called before translating; its error wraps `KindInvalidRequest`. `Request.Extensions` is an `Extension` with `Provider() string` — type-assert your own and reject another provider's.

Gotcha recorded in project/gotchas.md: a second `json.WithUnmarshalers` in a `JoinOptions` **replaces** the first. Join the funcs (`json.JoinUnmarshalers`), not the options, or the second interface dispatch silently never fires.

- StopNone (message_stop with no stop reason) is Done. The provider gave the loop nothing to act on; Result.StopReason carries the silence. Erroring would turn an omission into a failed run and resending would loop for ever.
- Every tool call the loop declines to run gets an IsError tool_result, not just cancelled ones: max_tokens, refusal, an unknown stop reason and a turn carrying tool calls without stopping for them all append the assistant message plus one error result per call as one unit. Invariant 9 is about the history being sendable; a conversation ending in a dangling tool_use is a 400 the moment anyone resumes it. - Both budget limits are checked at the TOP of the loop, before turn N is sent, so a turn the model asked for is always finished and committed: the conversation on a TurnLimit or TokenLimit stop is intact and resumable.
- Token accounting is TokensSpent(u) = u.TotalInput() + u.Output (reasoning is already inside Output).
- A deadline on the CALLER's context reads as StopCauseTimeout, not Cancelled — the cause really was a clock (context.Cause says so). Only an explicit cancel is Cancelled. The run's own Timeout uses context.WithTimeoutCause with an unexported sentinel.

Files: wire.go, wire_response.go, dialect.go, extensions.go, translate.go, messages.go, translate_response.go, plus dialect_test.go, translate_test.go, translate_response_test.go. `go test -race ./...` passes from the worktree.

DECISIONS TAKEN HERE (the client/stream leaf inherits them):

- Wire structs are UNEXPORTED (chatRequest, chatMessage, content, chatResponse, chatChunk, usage, wireError...). The package's public surface is Dialect/Quirks, Extensions and friends, Attribution, ProviderName. The client leaf builds bodies through translateRequest(req, dialect, stream) and reads them through translateResponse(*chatResponse) and translateUsage(*usage).
- Dialect zero value is OpenRouter (Dialect ""), matching CachePolicy/Effort house style. An unrecognised Dialect gets Generic's quirks — Quirks{} is the conservative answer, so the zero Quirks is also the safe one.
- Quirk table: OpenRouter = everything; OpenAI = reasoning_effort + metadata/user; LMStudio = reasoning_effort only; Generic = nothing beyond plain Chat Completions. Quirks.UsageCost is declared but not consumed by translateUsage: the translation reports whatever `cost` arrived. The client/models leaf can consult it to decide whether to fall back to the /models price list.
- One chatMessage struct serves both directions (role, content, tool_call_id, tool_calls, reasoning, reasoning_details, refusal, annotations); `content` is a typed union (null | string | parts) with its own marshal/unmarshal.
- Request.Metadata maps to the wire `metadata` object, sorted by key for invariant 8. The key "user_id" (Anthropic's spelling, and the example in Request.Metadata's own doc comment) is lifted to the top-level `user` member and removed from metadata. Both are gated on Quirks.Metadata.
- tool_choice is OMITTED for the zero value (auto), since auto is the wire default and some servers reject tool_choice with no tools. An unknown ToolChoiceMode passes through verbatim.
- Tool result -> role:"tool" message; content is the concatenated text of the result's text blocks; IsError is conveyed by the prefix "Error: " (const toolErrorPrefix); a non-text block inside a result becomes "[image]", "[document]", ... naming its block type.
- Unknown reasoning_details types (OpenRouter has added reasoning.server_tool_call) decode to goodall.Thinking{Raw: entry} with no Text — one re-emission path for every entry, rather than goodall.Unknown, which would need the wire rules written a second time on the way out.
- goodall.Unknown blocks in an assistant message are DROPPED on the way to the wire (their bytes are another provider's); so are images/documents/tool results in an assistant turn. Documented on translateRequest.
- Cache markers on blocks with no wire slot (assistant text, tool results, tool uses) are IGNORED rather than rejected, because a legitimate Anthropic-shaped conversation carries them and erroring would make cross-provider requests fail on OpenRouter. Only markers that become a content part count toward the four-breakpoint limit.
- Document filename = Document.Title, else "document". Image/Document with a SourceFile (provider file id) is rejected with KindInvalidRequest — this package uploads nothing.

FACTS RESOLVED FROM THE DOCS (previously UNVERIFIED or uncovered by research section 2):

- `reasoning.effort: "none"` is documented as disabling reasoning entirely; there is NO documented `enabled: false`. EffortOff therefore sends {"effort":"none"} on both the reasoning object and reasoning_effort. Source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/reasoning-tokens.md (WebFetch, 2026-09-15).
- `file.file_data` accepts a plain https URL as well as a base64 data: URL ("PDFs can be sent as direct URLs or base64-encoded data URLs"). A goodall.Document with a URL source is passed through as file_data. There is no `file_id` member in the PDF docs, so a provider file id is refused. Source: https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/pdfs.md (curl, 2026-09-15; note the path — /docs/features/multimodal/pdfs.md redirects there and /docs/overview/multimodal/pdfs.md is a 404).
- The live OpenAPI spec (https://openrouter.ai/openapi.json, fetched 2026-09-15) adds a FOURTH reasoning_details variant research section 2 does not list: `reasoning.server_tool_call {tool_name, arguments, result, tool_call_id, id, format, index}`. The wire struct admits it and it round-trips verbatim.
- ChatRequest carries a top-level `metadata` (map, max 16 pairs) and `user` (end-user id) alongside `session_id`, `debug`, `models`, `plugins`, `provider`, `cache_control`, `reasoning` and `reasoning_effort`. ProviderPreferences members confirmed: order, allow_fallbacks, require_parameters, only, ignore, quantizations, sort (price|throughput|latency|exacto), data_collection (allow|deny), zdr, max_price (prompt/completion/request/image as decimal STRINGS), enforce_distillable_text, preferred_max_latency, preferred_min_throughput.
- OpenAI's own published reasoning_effort enum could NOT be verified (platform.openai.com returns 403 to WebFetch). goodall sends its effort rung verbatim on the OpenAI dialect rather than clamping xhigh/max down to "high": clamping would quietly buy less thinking than the caller asked for, and the ladder keeps growing. If a strict OpenAI endpoint 400s on "xhigh", that is the right place to learn it.

FOR THE NEXT LEAF (client.go, stream.go, models.go, errors.go):

- chatChunk / streamChoice / messageDelta / toolCallDelta are already in wire_response.go, tested against a real-shaped frame, a trailing usage frame that repeats finish_reason, and a top-level error frame. wireError.Code is a jsontext.Value because the docs say it mirrors the HTTP status before commit and can be a provider string after; errorMetadata carries error_type, provider_name, provider_code and raw.
- translateUsage(*usage) (goodall.Usage, goodall.Cost) is the one function to call on the trailing usage chunk.
- Attribution.Headers() returns []Header{{HeaderReferer, ...}, {HeaderTitle, ...}}, skipping the empty half.

Files owned: hooks.go, resume.go, their tests, and the marked HOOK INSERTION POINTs in agent.go, run.go, run_tools.go (the loop leaf is closed, so this leaf owns the loop files now). - Hooks is a struct of nil-able funcs on Agent.Hooks; a nil func is a no-op. Every hook error ends the run with Stopped{Cause: StopCauseHook, Message: the error}.
- BeforeSend sees only the request parameters and the new, uncommitted turn: BeforeSend(ctx, req *Request, newTurn *Message) error, where req.Messages is empty during the hook and filled by the loop afterwards. The new turn is the user input on turn one and the tool-results message on later turns; it is committed to the conversation only after the hook returns nil, and always committed before any terminal event so the conversation stays intact.
- AfterReceive(ctx, *Response) error runs after a turn completes and before it is committed (the plan said *Message; the response carries the stop reason, which is what a hook acts on).
- BeforeToolCall(ctx, ToolUse) (Decision, error): Decision is a typed value built by Allow(), Deny(reason), Modify(input), Defer(). Deny yields an IsError result carrying the reason and the tool is not run. Modify runs the tool with the new input; the conversation keeps the model's original tool_use unchanged (history is what the model said). If ANY call of a turn is deferred, no tool of that turn runs: the assistant message is committed, the run ends with Stopped{Cause: StopCauseDeferred} and Result.Pending lists every tool_use of the turn.
- AfterToolCall(ctx, ToolUse, *ToolResult) error runs on each result before it is emitted and appended; the hook may shape the result (truncate, redact).
- Agent.Resume(ctx, conv Conversation, results ...ToolResult) Stream: the pending calls are the tool_use blocks of conv's last assistant message; a pending call with no result gets an IsError result saying none was provided, a result for an id that is not pending ends the run with Stopped Error KindInvalidRequest; the results are appended as one user message and the loop continues as Run with no new input (BeforeSend sees that message as the new turn).

Live findings (2026-09-15, or-stream leaf). One streamed and one blocking exchange on
anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 via OpenRouter (Amazon Bedrock upstream), plus three error probes
and GET /api/v1/models. Raw captures were kept in the scratchpad only; nothing with a key
is committed.

1. **`reasoning_details` streams as FRAGMENTS keyed by `index`, not as whole entries.** The
   docs (https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/best-practices/reasoning-tokens.md, "Each reasoning
   detail chunk is sent as it becomes available") read as whole entries; the wire disagrees.
   Observed: 30-odd chunks each carrying
   `{"type":"reasoning.text","text":"<fragment>","format":"anthropic-claude-v1","index":0}`,
   then a final fragment for the same index carrying only
   `{"type":"reasoning.text","signature":"Ess...","format":"anthropic-claude-v1","index":0}`.
   The entry has to be merged by `index` across chunks: `text`/`summary`/`data`/`signature`
   concatenate, every other member is last-writer-wins.

2. **The merged entry is byte-identical to the blocking path's.** Streaming fragments are
   `{type,text,format,index}` then `{type,signature,format,index}`; merging in first-seen
   member order yields `{type,text,format,index,signature}`, which is exactly the member order
   the blocking response returns. So the "Collect == Complete" criterion holds on real bytes,
   not only on synthesised fixtures.

3. **`delta.reasoning` duplicates `reasoning_details[].text` fragment for fragment.** Emitting
   thinking text from both would double it. The stream drives thinking from `reasoning_details`
   whenever they are present and falls back to `delta.reasoning` only when a chunk carries the
   flat string alone (a Generic/LMStudio server).

4. **`delta.content` is `""` or `null` on almost every chunk** (reasoning chunks, tool-call
   chunks, the finish chunk, the usage chunk). An empty content string must not open a text
   block or the message gains an empty Text block the blocking path does not have.

5. **Tool calls**: first fragment `{index,id,type,function:{name,arguments:""}}`, then fragments
   `{index,function:{arguments:"..."}}` with no id/name. Two calls interleave only by index
   order (0 finishes, then 1 starts) but the code keys by index regardless.

6. **The terminal pair**: a chunk with `finish_reason:"tool_calls"`, `native_finish_reason:
   "tool_use"` and an empty delta, then a chunk repeating both and carrying `usage` (with
   `cost`, `cost_details`, `service_tier` — unmodelled members, ignored), then `data: [DONE]`.
   No comment keep-alives appeared in a 4-second stream.

7. **The request id header is `x-generation-id`**, not `x-request-id`. `access-control-expose-
   headers` lists `X-Generation-Id,X-Provider-Name,request-id,cf-ray`, but only x-generation-id
   was actually set on the responses seen. internal/transport's `requestIDFrom` reads Request-Id
   then X-Request-Id, so it would have found nothing; the openrouter decoder reads X-Request-Id
   then X-Generation-Id itself. INTEGRATION NOTE below.

8. **Criterion 4's error, verified.** An image to a live text-only model
   (ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b) returns HTTP **404** with
   `{"error":{"message":"No endpoints found that support image input","code":404,"metadata":
   {"routing_funnel":[...],"failed_routing_step":"Filter by Image Support"}}}`.
   The metadata carries **no `error_type`**, so the message heuristic is load-bearing, and the
   message is capitalised, so the match is case-insensitive. A model with no live endpoints at
   all is the neighbouring message "No endpoints found for <model>." (also 404) and must stay
   KindNotFound; the heuristic therefore matches "no endpoints found that support", not "no
   endpoints found". An unknown model id is HTTP **400** `"... is not a valid model ID"` with
   `code: 400` — not 404 as one might guess.

9. **No usable per-model catalogue endpoint.** `GET /api/v1/models/{id}` is 404;
   `GET /api/v1/models/{id}/endpoints` returns a different shape with no `supported_parameters`,
   `top_provider` or `reasoning`. `Model(ctx, id)` therefore fetches `GET /models` (445 entries,
   `{data,total_count,links}`) and finds the id, which the loop's ModelInfo cache makes
   acceptable for v1.

10. **Catalogue facts checked across all 445 entries**: `reasoning` is present on 313 and its
    members are `mandatory` (313), `supported_efforts` (171), `default_effort` (171),
    `default_enabled` (151), `supports_max_tokens` (10). `pricing` members seen:
    prompt, completion (all 445), input_cache_read (277), input_cache_write (82),
    input_cache_write_1h (31), web_search, image, audio, internal_reasoning, overrides,
    image_output, audio_output, input_audio_cache. `architecture.input_modalities` uses
    "text", "image", "file", "audio", "video".

INTEGRATION NOTE (not my files): internal/transport/retry.go `requestIDFrom` could add
`X-Generation-Id` as a third fallback so a transport-level error on OpenRouter carries a
request id even when the provider decoder is not consulted. The openrouter decoder already
sets it, so nothing is broken today.

Hooks, approval and Resume built on wt/hooks (worktree .claude/worktrees/hooks). New: hooks.go (Hooks, Decision, Allow/Deny/Modify/Defer, the four nil-safe run helpers), resume.go (Agent.Resume, resumeTurn), hooks_test.go and resume_test.go (package goodall_test, 21 tests). Edited: agent.go (Agent.Hooks, a Resume pointer in Run's doc), run.go (the held new turn, BeforeSend, AfterReceive, Pending), run_tools.go (split into decide + runTools, Decision handling, AfterToolCall), stop.go (four result/stop texts), and a block-quote correction under "Hooks" in the architecture plan. `go fix`, `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go mod tidy` clean; `go test -count=3 -race ./...` passes.

Criteria, with the test that proves each:
- R0c (a BeforeToolCall error ends the run with Stopped and no tool executed) — TestBeforeToolCallErrorRunsNothing: Stopped{Hook}, the tool never ran, the hook was asked only about the first call, and the turn is committed with an error result per call so the conversation is still sendable.
- icz (Defer returns Pending tool uses and Resume continues to a Done result) — TestBeforeToolCallDeferPausesTheTurn plus TestDeferThenResumeReachesDone, end to end over one fake script: turn one defers (Pending in model order, no tool run, assistant turn committed with no results message), Resume hands back the approver's result, turn two answers, Done.
- 2eg (BeforeSend cannot alter an earlier message) — TestBeforeSendSeesOnlyTheNewTurn (req.Messages is empty during the hook on both turns) and TestBeforeSendCannotAlterAnEarlierMessage (what the hook appends to req.Messages reaches neither the wire nor the history). Both were mutation-checked: pre-filling req.Messages fails the first, and dropping the post-hook `req.Messages = r.conv.Messages()` fails the second.

Decisions taken beyond the dispatch rulings, all recorded in the plan's block quote:
- The run holds the new user turn UNCOMMITTED (run.newTurn) between prepare/runTools and the next BeforeSend, and commitNewTurn runs at the top of done(), stop(), fail() and commit(). So a budget stop, a hook error or a cancellation between turns still hands back a whole conversation, and the assistant turn can never be appended before the user turn it answers.
- AfterReceive runs before TurnEnd is emitted, but the turn's usage and cost are folded in whether or not it errors: the tokens were spent. Because it takes *Response, a hook can shape the response, and the loop acts on and commits what it left (TestAfterReceiveShapesTheResponse).
- A denied call emits ToolCallEnd and no ToolCallStart — ToolCallStart already documents itself as "about to run, after any hook has allowed it", and a denied call was never about to run. A deferred call emits neither. Tested.
- AfterToolCall runs on EVERY result the loop records for the turn, a denied call's error result included, so every ToolCallEnd has passed the shaping hook.
- On an AfterToolCall error the loop drains the rest of the turn's results (so the tools finish) but does NOT commit them: results that already passed the hook are kept, every other call gets "This tool ran, but its result was not kept…". Fail closed — committing unshaped results would defeat the redaction hook that just failed.
- Deny("") substitutes "This tool was not run: a hook refused the call."; an empty error result would leave the model retrying the same call. Written red first.

Integration notes for the chat leaf (MhK0aq): Agent.Hooks is a plain struct of nil-able funcs, so a chat service composes by assigning them; hooks are called on the run's goroutine one at a time. Resume(ctx, conv, results...) needs only the conversation from the deferred Stopped event — Result.Pending is a convenience for the UI, not an input. Pending is empty on every other exit. A resumed run is indistinguishable from any other run downstream: same events, same one terminal event, and BeforeSend sees the assembled results message as its newTurn.

Rulings made in code (the plan now carries a block quote recording them, under "The chat layer"):

- ThreadStore.Put writes the new Version and UpdatedAt back into the *Thread it was given; a thread at version 0 that does not exist is created, one at any other version that does not exist is ErrVersionConflict. List returns complete threads, UpdatedAt descending with id descending as tie-break (a total order, since ids are uuid v7). Delete has no version check.
- Subscribe's catch-up is the buffered events verbatim, not a synthesised MessageStart — a subscriber's Accumulator therefore rebuilds exactly the message an earlier subscriber holds. Verified by comparing the two rebuilt messages in TestSubscribeMidRunReplaysThenGoesLive.
- A subscriber that fills its bounded channel (DefaultSubscriberBuffer 256, WithSubscriberBuffer to change) is dropped and its stream ends with ErrSubscriberOverflow; the run is never paced by a client.
- A finished run's events are NOT retained: Subscribe on a thread with no run in flight yields nothing and ends. This means Send-then-Subscribe on one goroutine can miss a very fast run; documented on Subscribe, and the CLI example should be aware of it. Retention would be a cache with no eviction, so it was left out.
- Persist happens before the thread is released and before subscriptions close, on context.WithoutCancel(service ctx) — a stopped run reaches persistence with its own context already cancelled. One ErrVersionConflict retry against a re-read thread, then log and give up.
- Sentinels: ErrThreadNotFound, ErrVersionConflict (store.go); ErrThreadBusy, ErrThreadIdle, ErrServiceClosed, ErrNotResolvable, ErrSubscriberOverflow (service.go). Stop on an idle thread is ErrThreadIdle, not a no-op. Create and Get keep working after Shutdown; Send and Resolve answer ErrServiceClosed.
- Options are WithLogger, WithBudget (copies the agent rather than mutating the caller's) and WithSubscriberBuffer.

data.title: Send-then-Subscribe race: rule on run retention or Send returning a stream
data.description: Found by the chat-service leaf (2026-09-15). Service.Send returns once the run is registered, Subscribe on a thread with no run in flight yields nothing, and a finished run's events are not retained. So a caller that does Send then Subscribe on one goroutine, the CLI shape the plan describes, sees nothing at all if the run finished in between: invisible against a real provider (microseconds against hundreds of milliseconds), a coin flip against the fake or a cache hit. Options: (a) Send returns the run's stream as well as its id, so the starter is attached before the run begins; (b) retain each thread's last run's events until the next Send, so a late Subscribe replays it; (c) Subscribe takes a run id and answers a not-found error for a finished one, so the caller reads the thread. (a) is the smallest and serves the CLI directly; (b) also serves a web client that reloads just after the answer finished. Decide before the CLI and web examples are built.

Rulings before dispatch (2026-09-15, third build session):

1. ModelInfo reaches a provider's translation through a new field, Request.ModelInfo *ModelInfo, which the loop fills from the catalogue and a direct consumer may fill by hand; nil means "not consulted". Translation stays a pure function of the Request, and a provider's Stream never makes a hidden catalogue call. The Anthropic translator reads Capabilities.ThinkingStyle when it is Adaptive or Budget and falls back to the name heuristic otherwise; the always-on (fable) reading of the heuristic still applies on top, since the catalogue does not say a model refuses "disabled".

2. The memo lives on the provider clients, not on Agent: anthropic.Client and openrouter.Client memoise Model() per id under a mutex (successes only; OpenRouter caches the one catalogue fetch, so every model is served by it). Agent is a plain struct that chat.NewService copies by value, so a mutex or atomic on it is a vet failure and a split cache. ModelLister's doc says the agent calls Model at the start of every run and an implementation should memoise. The two existing doc comments that say "the agent caches it" are corrected.

3. The pre-flight fetches once per run (before the first turn, when the provider implements ModelLister) and checks every turn's request before it is sent: Image blocks need CapImageInput, application/pdf Documents need CapPDFInput, a non-empty tool list needs CapTools, a thinking effort other than Default/Off needs CapThinking, CacheManual markers need CapCacheControl. Only Unsupported refuses; Unknown lets it through. A refusal ends the run with Stopped{Cause: StopCauseError, Kind: KindUnsupportedInput, Message: capErr.Error()} before any HTTP call, with the new turn committed as every other stop does. A catalogue error (NotFound included) is logged at Warn and the run proceeds with no ModelInfo, because the catalogue can lag the API; no negative caching in v1.

MaxOutput from the catalogue does NOT override max_tokens this leaf: Anthropic refuses a non-streaming request whose max_tokens implies more than ten minutes of generation, so sending a 128k cap on Complete would break the blocking path. The view is computed by an exported pure function over a Thread plus the two facts the thread does not carry (whether the agent has a system prompt, and the agent's ThinkingDisplay); Service.View(ctx, threadID) reads the thread from the store and calls it. It reflects the stored thread, as Get does; a run in flight is watched through Subscribe.

2. Content: user text and media, assistant text, thinking text unless the agent's display is DisplayOmitted, redacted thinking as a marker with no text, tool calls as name plus an input placeholder, tool results as a placeholder plus status (ok/error), and a system placeholder when the agent has a system prompt. 4. Wire writers: WriteSSE(w io.Writer, events goodall.Stream) error and WriteNDJSON(w io.Writer, events goodall.Stream) error. What was built, and the decisions inside the rulings:

1. `NewThreadView(thread *Thread, opts ViewOptions) *ThreadView` is the pure function; the two agent facts travel in a small options struct, `ViewOptions{HasSystemPrompt bool, ThinkingDisplay goodall.ThinkingDisplay}`. The prompt *text* is deliberately not a parameter — what cannot be passed in cannot be leaked out — so `Service.View` passes `s.agent.System != ""`. A nil thread has no view, mirroring `Thread.Clone`.

2. `Service.View(ctx, threadID)` lives in chat/view.go rather than service.go and reads the store exactly as `Get` does; nothing is ever written back.

3. Wire shape: `ThreadView{id, system, messages[], usage, cost, version, created_at, updated_at}`, `MessageView{role, content[], partial}`, `BlockView{kind, text, media, tool_use_id, tool_name, status, block_type, placeholder}` with `BlockViewKind` one of text/image/document/tool_call/tool_result/thinking/redacted_thinking/unknown, and `MediaView{source, media_type, url, file_id, title, placeholder}`. `ToolResultStatus` is ok/error. `System` is the placeholder id, empty when the agent has no prompt. The `tool_use_id` is carried on both the call and its result so a UI can pair them — it names the call, not its content. Thinking signatures, redacted-thinking payloads and `Unknown.Raw` have no field at all, so they cannot travel.

4. Placeholder ids: `hex(sha256(threadID + "\x00" + position))[:32]`, position being `msgIndex "\x00" blockIndex` or the literal `system`. Digesting position rather than content is what keeps an id from being a verifier for a guessed secret, and from advertising that two threads hold the same tool result.

5. `WriteSSE` / `WriteNDJSON` share one body (`writeStream`) over a `frameWriter`, so the ending, the error frame and the flushing cannot drift between the formats. `EventError` (a `goodall.EventType` constant of "error") names the failure frame; `WireError{type,message,code}` is the payload and `WireErrorCode` is `subscriber_overflow` or `stream_error`. A stream error returns nil — it reached the client — and only a write failure is returned (wrapped, so `errors.Is` finds the transport error). No `id:` lines and no catch-up marker.

6. Flushing uses a locally declared `interface{ Flush() }` rather than importing net/http, so the chat layer does not pull net/http into a CLI consumer's binary; the shape is `http.Flusher`'s exactly, and `bufio.Writer` (whose Flush returns an error) deliberately does not match.

Findings worth keeping:

- In encoding/json/v2 a nil slice marshals as `[]`, not `null`, so `Blocks(nil)` round-trips back as `Blocks{}`. That broke the first draft of the round-trip test (a `TurnEnd` whose `Response.Message` had no content), not the writers. Any test asserting `reflect.DeepEqual` over decoded events must avoid nil slices in its fixtures.
- The SSE multi-line `data:` guard cannot be exercised through `WriteSSE`, because json/v2 output is always one line; it is asserted directly in `chat/wire_internal_test.go` (the only in-package test file in chat) so the guard is not dead code nobody has run.
- `Subscribe` returns a lazily-attaching stream: a test that hands `svc.Subscribe(...)` straight to a writer can race the run to its end. The deterministic shape is to attach with the existing `subscription` helper, read to a known event, and then hand the *rest* of the pull to the writer (`(*subscription).stream()` in wire_test.go).

Catalogue wired into the loop (branch wt/loop-preflight, agent loop-preflight).

What landed. `Request.ModelInfo *ModelInfo` is the seam: `run.execute` reads the catalogue once, before the first turn, through `run.lookupModel` (a provider that is not a ModelLister gets nothing; a lookup error, KindNotFound included, is logged at Warn and the run goes on with nil), and `run.request` puts it on every turn's Request. `preflight.go` holds `checkCapabilities(req) *CapabilityError`, a pure function of the Request that the loop calls each turn after BeforeSend and before the send; a refusal ends the run with `Stopped{StopCauseError, KindUnsupportedInput}` with the new turn committed and no HTTP call made. Anthropic's `thinkingFor` now takes the whole `*goodall.Request` and chooses its style through the new `styleFor(model, info)`: the catalogue's Adaptive/Budget beats the name heuristic, and a name that reads as always-on (fable) survives a catalogue "adaptive", since the catalogue never says a model refuses `disabled`. Both clients memoise `Model()` per id under a mutex, successes only; OpenRouter stores every entry of the one catalogue fetch, under the id and the canonical slug, so the first lookup answers for all of them. `loop_cost.go` was not created: cost accumulation is already `r.cost` in run.go and nothing new belonged in a file of its own.

(3) The pre-flight runs per turn on purpose — a tool result can carry an image the caller's first message did not. Built examples/cli on wt/cli-example (worktree .claude/worktrees/cli-example). Four files: main.go (flags, provider, signal wiring), repl.go (Loop over io.Reader/io.Writer), print.go (the event renderer), dice.go (the one built-in tool), plus repl_test.go (five tests against internal/fake).

Shape, as ruled: main.go holds no logic beyond flags and wiring; `Loop(ctx, *chat.Service, io.Reader, io.Writer, Options{ThreadID, Prompt, Interrupt})` is what the tests drive through an io.Pipe. Only goodall, goodall/anthropic, goodall/chat and goodall/openrouter are imported outside the test file. Keys come from ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY and the -h text says `source .env` loads them. Default models are named constants dated 2026-09-15: claude-sonnet-5 (matching internal/livemodel.Anthropic) and anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 (the id openrouter/testdata/models.json carries). -thinking takes the Effort names with "default" for the zero value, and any effort other than "off" also asks for DisplaySummarized.

Rendering is plain text with no terminal library: text deltas verbatim, thinking under a "[thinking]" line with every line prefixed "  | " (the prefix is applied by the writer, since a delta breaks anywhere), "[tool] name {input}" when a call starts and "[tool] name ok|error: result" when it ends, "[usage] turn N: X in, Y out" per TurnEnd with the cost appended only when Cost.Reported, and "[stopped] the answer was cut short; what had arrived is kept in the thread" on a Stopped whose Cause is cancelled.

Both criteria are met. (1) Live smoke runs on 2026-09-15 against both providers, two exchanges each (a question and a dice roll): Anthropic streamed a summarized thinking block on default effort and reported tokens only; OpenRouter reported cost per turn (0.00083457 USD on the first turn). Transcripts are in the session report. (2) TestLoopStopsMidAnswerAndTheNextTurnContinues drives a fake Stalled turn, fires the same interrupt channel Ctrl-C feeds, waits for the cut-short line, then sends a second line: the thread ends with the complete second answer and carries the Partial assistant message "starting to answer". Mutation-checked — with the svc.Stop call removed the test fails on the missing cut-short line rather than passing anyway.

Two things worth carrying forward. The loop must read Send's Run.Events to the very *end* of the stream, not stop at the terminal event: the service persists the thread and releases it as the stream closes, so a client that breaks out early races its own next Send into ErrThreadBusy. And Ctrl-C at the prompt has to be answerable while a read is blocked on a terminal nobody is typing at, so the line reader runs on its own goroutine and the loop selects over lines, the interrupt and ctx.

The public API needed no changes and no workarounds; the one seam that is easy to get wrong is the stream-to-the-end rule above.

chat/redact.go: Redact(events goodall.Stream, opts ViewOptions) goodall.Stream, a pure mapping. Every yielded event is one of goodall's own types with fields zeroed — goodall.Event is sealed, so the chat layer cannot mint a redacted event type. goodall.AgentTool(child *Agent, name, description string, opts...) (Tool, error) in the

data.title: Nested events and per-call accounting
data.description:
The one core change delegation asks for. Design against the two adapters that now
exist: an optional interface a tool may implement to emit events during Execute,
wrapped by the loop as ToolEvent{ToolUseID, Event} in the parent stream; optional
Usage and Cost on ToolCallEnd for what the call itself spent; a cost-only roll-up on
Result (tokens across providers are not commensurable, money is), reported only when
every contributor reported. Budgets stay on the parent's own tokens. chat.Redact
must decide what of a nested event travels. Rule on the shape first, as a note on this
leaf, then build.

data.text:
Rulings before dispatch (2026-09-17, main thread):

- Package name `typesafe`; env key TYPESAFE_API_KEY (present in .env); default base URL https://api.typesafe.ai; default model "jev-latest"; model for fixtures and live tests pinned in internal/livemodel as the versioned id `jev-1.13.0` so thresholds asserted in tests do not move under an alias.
- Wire facts are documentation only until the recorder runs: see project/2026-09-17-typesafe-jev-findings.md "The wire". Record first, then write decode tests against the recordings; if the live shape differs from the findings, correct the findings in place as a marked block quote.
- The recorder's existing `complete()` helper takes a goodall.Completer, which this client is not. The typesafe exchanges use `rec.httpClient()` through `typesafe.WithHTTPClient` and `rec.save(name, "json")` directly; nothing else in the recorder changes.
- Cost: not reported (no per-response cost member). Usage maps input_tokens/output_tokens onto goodall.Usage.
- No streaming: one blocking call, one JSON body. Not a goodall.Provider and not a Completer.
- Ordered types everywhere the wire has a map: Questions []NamedQuestion{ID, Question}, Choice.Options []Option{Key, Description}; answers' probabilities may decode into a map since they are read, not sent — but expose an ordered accessor if it costs nothing.

Rulings before dispatch (2026-09-17, main thread):

- Root package, one file pair: agent_tool.go and agent_tool_test.go. No change to run.go, run_tools.go, hooks.go or the event set; the accounting leaf (fH6YmO) owns those.
- Signature: `func AgentTool(child *Agent, name, description string) (Tool, error)`; the input schema is one required string parameter `prompt` (use NewTool's inference over a struct so the schema and the required check are the loop's own). Registration errors match NewTool's: a bad name, a nil child.
- The child runs `child.Run(ctx, Conversation{}, Text{Text: prompt})` on the ctx Execute is given, so the parent's cancellation and timeout reach it. The result is the final assistant message's text blocks joined; a Done with no text is an empty TextResult, not an error.
- A child that ends in Stopped is an IsError result whose text carries the Cause and Message, so the parent model can decide what to do; a Stopped with Pending (a Defer inside the child) is the same, with the text saying approval inside a delegated run is not supported yet.
- The child's events are not forwarded and its usage is not reported. Say so in the doc comment and point at the accounting leaf.
- The child Agent value is copied at construction (it holds no per-run state, invariant 12) so a later change to the caller's struct does not reach a running tool.

Built AgentTool in the root package (branch worktree-agent-a040e0683ef2df0d4). Three new files, nothing else touched: agent_tool.go, agent_tool_test.go, agent_tool_example_test.go.

Shape as ruled: `AgentTool(child *Agent, name, description string) (Tool, error)`, built on NewTool over an unexported `delegatedTask{Prompt string}` so the schema, the required check and the bad-input text are the loop's own. The name is validated first (so a call with two mistakes reports the one NewTool would), then a nil child is refused; the child Agent is copied by value at construction — Agent holds no mutex and no per-run state, confirmed field by field. Execute runs `child.Run(ctx, Conversation{}, Text{Text: prompt})` on the ctx it was given. Done → TextResult of the final assistant message's non-empty text blocks joined with "\n\n" (empty when the child wrote nothing, and an empty TextResult rather than an error). Stopped → ErrorResult naming the cause and carrying the child's Message, with a second sentence when Result.Pending is non-empty saying approval inside a delegated run is not supported yet. The only Go error is a *ProtocolError for a run stream with no terminal event. The doc comment states that the child's events are not forwarded and its usage and cost are reported nowhere, and names the accounting task.

BRIEF ERROR worth recording: Stream.CollectResult cannot implement this. It returns only the Result, and a Stopped's Cause, Message and Kind live on the *event*, not in the Result it carries — Result has StopReason and Pending but no cause — so CollectResult cannot tell Done from Stopped at all. runDelegate ranges the child stream itself and keeps the terminal event; a comment in agent_tool.go says why. Nothing in stream.go changed. If the accounting leaf wants this shared, the natural move is a `Stream.Terminal() (Event, error)` beside CollectResult.

Tests (8, all against internal/fake, red first — the first run failed to build on "undefined: goodall.AgentTool"): the delegation itself (the parent's second request carries a tool_result with the child's two text blocks joined, and the child was asked the prompt the parent wrote); a Done with no text as an empty plain result; cancellation of the parent while the child is parked on fake.Stalled (parent's terminal event is Canceled, the child's provider stream was unwound); a Broken child as an IsError result carrying cause and message; a child whose BeforeToolCall Defers as an IsError result saying approval is unsupported; the child's events absent from the parent's stream (one ToolCallStart, two TurnStarts, one Done, with the child itself running a tool over two turns); a nil child and three invalid names refused at construction.

Since every test was green on the first run after implementing, four mutations were applied and reverted one at a time to prove each assertion bites: joining the child's text with "" (delegation test fails), TextResult in place of ErrorResult for Stopped (both error tests fail), dropping the Pending sentence (defer test fails), and running the child on context.Background() instead of the tool's ctx (the cancellation test times out at 25s instead of passing).

`go fix ./...`, gofmt over the tracked files, `go vet ./...`, `go mod tidy`, `go build ./...` and `go test -short -race ./...` all clean; go.mod untouched.

README not edited per the briefing. Proposed line for the customizer quick start, after "The tool's JSON schema is inferred from the handler's input type.": "`goodall.AgentTool` wraps a second agent — another model, another provider — as a tool, so a model can delegate a task and read its answer; the delegated run inherits the caller's cancellation and keeps its own budget."

Two facts from the agent-as-tool leaf (4LOjsN, merged as 342e304) that this design should take into account:

1. Stream.CollectResult returns only *Result, and a Stopped's Cause, Message and Kind live on the event, so a consumer that needs to tell Done from Stopped (a delegate, a nested-event forwarder) has to range the stream and keep the terminal event. runDelegate in agent_tool.go does that privately. data.text:
Built `goodall/typesafe` on branch worktree-agent-a3770f708dda00f19. Offline suite green
(`go test -short -race ./...`), live test green against the real API.

Surface as settled in code:

- `New(apiKey string, opts ...ClientOption) *Client` — `WithBaseURL`, `WithHTTPClient`,
  `WithMaxRetries`. **The option type is `ClientOption`, not `Option`**: the brief and the
  findings sketch gave the name `Option` to both the constructor option and a `Choice`'s
  option, which does not compile. The domain type kept `Option` (it is the API's word and
  appears in every call site); the constructor type pairs with the `AskOption` that already
  existed. The two provider packages keep `Option` for theirs.
- `Ask(ctx, state any, questions Questions, opts ...AskOption) (*Answers, error)`,
  `WithModel`, `Models(ctx) ([]ModelCard, error)`, `ModelCard.Released() (time.Time, error)`.
- `QuestionType` (`TypeNoul`/`TypeChoice`/`TypeScore`), sealed `Question` with `Noul`,
  `Choice{Options []Option}`, `Score{Levels []string}`; `Questions []NamedQuestion{ID,
  Question}` marshaling as the questions object in slice order and unmarshaling back in
  document order (the authored-questions tool needs the decode side).
- Sealed `Answer` with `NoulAnswer`, `ChoiceAnswer`, `ScoreAnswer`, `UnknownAnswer`;
  `Outcome`, `ChoiceAnswer.Ranked()`, `ScoreAnswer.Ranked()`, `ScoreAnswer.Levels()`,
  `NoulAnswer.Yes(threshold)`; `Answers` with `Model`, `Usage`, `Cost` (never reported),
  `All`, `IDs`, `Lookup`, `Noul`/`Choice`/`Score` and `*AnswerError{ID, Want, Got}`.
  `Answers` round-trips through JSON, which is what the tool adapter's result needs.

Fixtures recorded 2026-09-17 against `jev-1.13.0` into `typesafe/testdata`
(`mixed` 448/73, `noul_criteria` 328/23, `models`, `refused` HTTP 422).

Three things for the adapters leaf (Tfq6cs):

1. **The API has a fourth question type, `bounding_box`, that the published reference does
   not list.** The real 422 names it among its expected tags. `AuthoredTool` must refuse it
   rather than pass it through, since this package models neither its request nor its answer
   members; an answer of that type already decodes to `UnknownAnswer`.
2. `Questions` decodes from JSON and rejects an unknown type with an error naming the id and
   the three types it knows — that is the "rejects an unknown question type" half already
   done; the schema for the model to fill is still yours.
3. `Answers` marshals back to the wire shape with the ids in the order they arrived, so
   `goodall.JSONResult(answers)` round-trips into `Answers` unchanged.

Findings doc corrected in place: the "no live call was made" premise, and a block quote at
the end of "The wire" with the four observed differences (bounding_box, the FastAPI-shaped
422 detail list, `release_date` as an RFC 3339 timestamp under a `models` wrapper, answer
member order).

README rows were not added — the brief reserved that for integration.

Rulings before dispatch (2026-09-17, main thread), on top of the leaf description:

- The client landed as 876d77a; its surface is typesafe/doc.go, client.go, questions.go, answer.go, answers.go. Questions and Answers both round-trip through JSON (Questions.UnmarshalJSONFrom refuses an unknown type naming the id; Answers marshals as the API sends it), which is the seam the tools use.
- The API serves a fourth question type, bounding_box, that the client does not model (typesafe/testdata/live_refused.json names it). AuthoredTool must refuse it, and any other unknown type, with an IsError result naming the id and the three types it accepts; the Questions decoder already does this, so the tool's job is to surface that error as a result rather than a Go error.
- Guidance placement (owner ruling, 2026-09-17): first-party, concise, and where the model is looking when it acts. The authored tool's description carries three or four sentences: what Jev is for (fast typed judgments over a state, many questions per call), what it cannot do (generate text, count, compare numbers or dates, read pixels), and the habit to break (ask everything in one call). The per-field guidance goes in the `desc` tags of the input schema: on instructions ("state the exact condition; the model reads literally"), on choice options ("name every option and add a none-of-the-above when the list might not cover the input"), on score levels ("each level describes a concrete situation"), on state ("only the material the questions need"). Nothing goes in the system prompt by default. Export the description text as constants and take a WithDescription-style option so a consumer can override it; test behavior, never wording.
- The fixed-questions Tool needs almost none of that: its description is the consumer's, saying what the judgment is.
- Tool results: goodall.JSONResult(answers) so the result decodes back into typesafe.Answers; the result text is the answers JSON and nothing else.
- Route: a helper for Hooks.BeforeSend. It reads the new turn's text blocks (newTurn may be nil, in which case it does nothing), asks Jev, and hands the Answers to a consumer callback `func(ctx, req *Request, newTurn *Message, answers *Answers) error` that may shape the request or return an error to refuse the turn. Route never edits earlier turns (invariant 1) and never puts the system prompt into the state.
- A live check is part of this leaf: one real run of AuthoredTool through a real conversational model (anthropic, livemodel.Anthropic) with a realistic task, logging the questions the model wrote so a reader can judge them against the jaggedness list; skip loudly without both keys. It is an observation, not an assertion on wording.
- Cost: Answers.Cost is always unreported; do not pretend otherwise in the tool result.

Built the three adapters in goodall/typesafe, no root change (branch worktree-agent-a67419308bea3074a).

New files: typesafe/tool.go (Tool, ToolOption, WithToolModel, WithDescription, the shared judge/refusal path), typesafe/tool_authored.go (AuthoredTool and the model-written question shape), typesafe/route.go (Route, Decide, RouteOption, WithRouteModel, WithState, WithFallthrough), typesafe/guidance.go (DefaultAuthoredDescription), plus tool_test.go, tool_authored_test.go, route_test.go, adapters_example_test.go (one example per constructor) and live_authored_test.go. typesafe/doc.go gained a section naming the three adapters; the findings doc gained an Observed block quote for the live run.

Rulings taken, for the record:

- **`WithModel` was already taken** by the client's per-call AskOption, so the construction-time options are `WithToolModel` and `WithRouteModel`, documented as the tool- and route-level spelling of it. Renaming the AskOption would have been a change to the client leaf's files.
- **The state is one required `jsontext.Value` member.** It infers to one described member accepting a string, an object or an array, which is the sentence the API's own `state` writes. The alternative — a string field beside an object field — needs "exactly one of these", which the schema both providers accept cannot say, and makes the model choose a field before it writes anything.
- **Route fails closed by default.** A router that silently stopped routing sends every turn to whichever model the agent was built with and says nothing; `WithFallthrough()` is the opt-in for consumers whose routing is an optimization. A definition mistake in a Route (nil client, unaskable questions, nil decide) is reported by the first run, because a `Hooks` field is a func with nowhere to return an error at construction.
- **`Decide` is a named exported type** rather than the inline func signature in the brief, so the contract about req.Messages and about refusing a turn has a doc comment of its own.
- **A live refusal is logged, not failed.** One of three live runs refused its first call and succeeded on its second, which is the guard working; the live test asserts that at least one call produced a judgment.

data.text:
Design ruled 2026-09-17 (main thread), recorded as a dated block quote under Decisions in project/2026-09-14-architecture-plan.md; that block quote is the authority. Summary:

1. Optional interface beside Tool (suggested name Reporter, method ExecuteReporting(ctx, input jsontext.Value, report func(Event)) (ToolResult, Usage, Cost, error) — or a small ToolOutcome struct instead of the three values; settle the spelling in code and say why). The loop runs a tool that implements it through this method instead of Execute. Every reported event is wrapped as ToolEvent{ToolUseID, Name, Event} (wire tag "tool_event", sealed Event, JSON round trip in event_json.go) and emitted on the parent stream by the run goroutine, in report order, before that call's ToolCallEnd. yield is not goroutine-safe, so reports from tool goroutines must be funneled to the run goroutine: the results loop in run_tools.go selects on the finished channel and a reports channel. report must never block the run's unwinding: after the consumer breaks or the run is canceled, a report is dropped (select on the send and on a closed "stopped" channel), and the deferred wg.Wait must still complete.
2. ToolCallEnd gains Usage Usage `json:"usage,omitzero"` and Cost Cost `json:"cost,omitzero"`, filled from the reporting method's return. A plain Execute tool leaves both zero.
3. No roll-up on Result (reason in the plan). Budget unchanged.
4. chat.Redact: a ToolEvent is redacted by recursing redactEvent on the inner event, keeping ToolUseID and Name; a dropped inner event (ToolInputDelta) drops the wrapper. Usage and Cost on ToolCallEnd pass through (money and tokens are what a front end bills on).
5. AgentTool implements the interface: forwards every child event through report, returns the child's Result.Usage and Result.Cost. typesafe.Tool and AuthoredTool implement it: report nothing, return answers.Usage and answers.Cost (unreported). Route is untouched.
6. examples/cli renders a ToolEvent one level indented (a preview for the new state); examples/web may ignore it.
7. Stream.Terminal() (Event, error) beside CollectResult is optional; add it only if AgentTool's forwarding loop is cleaner with it.

Built on branch worktree-agent-a35d6643cf4a06531 (not committed). The ruling held; everything below is how it landed in code, and the plan now carries an "Added 2026-09-17 while building the nested events" block quote under **The loop** with the same four points.

SPELLING. `Reporter` with `ExecuteReporting(ctx, input, report func(Event)) (ToolOutcome, error)`, and `ToolOutcome{Result, Usage, Cost}`. The method cannot be a second `Execute` — an implementation is a `Tool` too — and the struct rather than three returns keeps a later fact about a call from editing every signature.

BEYOND THE BRIEF, and the one thing to review: `NewReportingTool[In]` is exported beside `NewTool`. `typesafe` is a different package, so it cannot reach an unexported constructor, and hand-rolling Name/Description/Schema/Execute there would duplicate the schema inference, the required-member check and the input-error prose. `tool.go` grew a shared `toolDefinition[In]` (name, description, schema, decode) that `typedTool` and the new `reportingTool` embed; `typedTool.Execute` is unchanged in behavior. `reportingTool.Execute` runs the same handler with the reports discarded, for a caller who runs a tool by hand.

WIRE. Tag `tool_event`, `ToolEvent{ToolUseID, Name, Event}`, sealed, `FromLoop() == true` so the accumulator ignores it. `decodeEvent` now decodes every event body with the joined event-and-block unmarshalers instead of the block ones alone, which is what lets a ToolEvent nest to any depth through the one table; because that dispatch is recursive, `eventUnmarshalers` is assigned in `init` — a declaration initializer whose function reaches the variable again is an initialization cycle the compiler refuses. Round trips are asserted at one and two levels.

CONCURRENCY. `runTools` selects on an unbuffered `reports chan ToolEvent` beside `done`. Unbuffered is load-bearing: a report is handed over only when the run goroutine takes it, so it reaches the stream before the reporting call's ToolCallEnd and in report order. A report is dropped, never waited on, in two cases — the consumer left (a `stopped` channel closed on the way out of runTools, deferred *after* `wg.Wait` so it closes first) and the call already returned (a per-call `returned` channel, tested before the send so a late report is dropped even while the turn's other calls are still reporting). Once an AfterToolCall hook has failed, reports are drained and dropped: the work they describe is being discarded with the run.

MUTATION CHECKS (both reverted). Replacing the guarded send with a plain `reports <- …` makes TestReportsAfterTheConsumerLeavesAreDroppedAndTheRunUnwinds fail on its 5s timeout ("breaking out of the run hung on a tool that kept reporting"). Dropping the `returned` pre-check makes TestAReportAfterTheToolReturnedIsDropped fail with two tool events where one was wanted, 3 times out of 3.

ACCOUNTING. `ToolCallEnd` gained `Usage` and `Cost` (`omitzero`), filled from the outcome; a plain Execute tool leaves both zero, and a Reporter that errors keeps whatever it said it spent, because the tokens were spent. No roll-up on Result, Budget untouched, both asserted.

ADAPTERS. AgentTool forwards every child event, terminal one included, and returns the child Result's Usage and Cost; its "two things a nested run does not yet do" paragraph is replaced. `typesafe.Tool`/`AuthoredTool` report nothing and return `answers.Usage` with the unreported `answers.Cost`; a question set refused before the network declares nothing.

REDACTION. `chat.Redact` recurses on the inner event, keeps ToolUseID and Name, drops the wrapper when the inner event is dropped (ToolInputDelta) or nil, and passes Usage and Cost on ToolCallEnd through. chat/view.go and the subscription path needed nothing — neither switches on event types.

EXAMPLES. examples/cli renders a ToolEvent through a child printer writing via a new `indentWriter`, four spaces in, and takes the child's line state back so the parent's next label starts on its own line. examples/web's browser switch gained a comment saying a `tool_event` is ignored on purpose.

TESTS. New: run_reporting_test.go (6 tests), examples/cli/print_test.go (2). Extended: event_json_test.go (a ToolCallEnd carrying usage, a tool_event, a doubly nested tool_event, the 18-type guard, the classification table), accumulate_test.go, agent_tool_test.go (the "keeps the child's events out" test became "forwards the child's events wrapped", plus a usage test), typesafe/tool_test.go, typesafe/tool_authored_test.go, chat/redact_test.go (4 new). Red first: the suite failed to build across four packages on the first run.

VERIFIED: `go fix ./...`, `gofmt -l .` (clean), `go vet ./...`, `go mod tidy`, `go build ./...`, `go test -short -race ./...` twice plus `-count 5` over the four touched packages, `agents check`. No new dependency; deps_test.go passes unchanged.
