data.text:
Measured. The claim survives, but only where the call is close, and the first attempt nearly hid that.

`scripts/probe-option-order` asks one Choice question about one fixed ticket through `typesafe.Client.Ask`, n samples with the options as authored and n with the slice reversed, and verifies the input: it logs every request body through an `http.RoundTripper` installed with `WithHTTPClient`, decodes the option order back out of the sent bytes through `typesafe.Questions`, and refuses a run whose samples within an arm are not byte-identical. Both runs below reported 739/624-byte bodies identical within each arm and reversed across arms, so the only thing that moved was the option order.

Run A, `go run ./scripts/probe-option-order -env /Users/ben/git/goodall/.env -n 3 -model jev-1.13.0 -state ambiguous`. Every sample answered by `jev-1.13.0` (from `Answers.Model`). Probabilities billing/technical/sales:
- forward (billing, technical, sales): 0.86/0.01/0.13, 0.85/0.01/0.14, 0.86/0.01/0.13; confidence 0.79, 0.78, 0.79
- reverse (sales, technical, billing): 0.78/0.02/0.20, 0.75/0.02/0.23, 0.72/0.02/0.26; confidence 0.68, 0.62, 0.57
- noise floor (widest same-order spread) 0.06 on billing; cross-order spread 0.14 on billing. Cross exceeds noise by 0.08, and the two arms do not overlap on any of the three options.

Run B, the control, same command with `-state plain` (a plainly-billing ticket): forward 0.98/0.02/0.00, 0.98/0.02/0.00, 0.97/0.03/0.00; reverse 0.98/0.02/0.00 three times. Noise floor 0.01, cross-order spread 0.01 — nothing.

Direction: in both arms the option listed *first* gains weight (billing 0.86 -> 0.72-0.78 when moved last; sales 0.13 -> 0.20-0.26 when moved first). An earlier run on byte-identical input to run A (before `-state` existed) gave forward 0.87/0.88/0.88 and reverse 0.75/0.75/0.78, so across twelve samples the forward billing values (0.85-0.88) and the reverse ones (0.72-0.78) do not overlap.

What this does not show: one state, one model version, three samples per arm, and no attempt at a per-option regression. It shows the effect is real on a close call and invisible on an easy one, not how large it is in general.

Method note worth keeping: the first attempt used a plainly-billing ticket and returned 0.98/0.02/0.00 in both arms — a saturated distribution has nowhere for an order effect to show, and reporting that 0.0000 as "no effect" would have been a definitional zero. Both states now ship behind `-state` so both figures are reproducible.

Cost: 6 billed calls per run, 2706 and 2568 input tokens, $0.000114 and $0.000108 at TypeSafe's published $0.042 per million input tokens. Four runs in all (two exploratory), well under a cent.

data.text:
Design settled before code, against the plan's Design section and the APIs on main.

Shape: main.go parses options and builds deps (providers, judge client) from the
environment; agent.go assembles the parent agent, its five tools and the route and
streams a run; store.go holds the inbox (the Records read once at startup) and the
in-memory run store the tools write to; report.go renders the plain-text report from
it. Three agents means three provider slots in deps, identical in production and three
separate internal/fake providers in the offline test.

Three judgments about seams, each a departure from the letter of the brief:

1. check_draft is a goodall.NewReportingTool that calls Client.Ask itself, not a
   typesafe.Tool. A typesafe.Tool's state is authored by the model, so the model would
   have to echo the sender, subject and snippet into the judge's state — the exact
   habit the plan removes from triage_inbox ("the model names records, it does not echo
   them") — and there is no seam between the judge's answers and the tool result where
   code could apply the four thresholds or record the verdict for the report. The tool

data.title: Strict tool schemas, opt-in per tool, on both providers
data.description:
**Why.** Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Fable 5.1 reject a forced `tool_choice` (`any` or a named tool) with a 400, and goodall refuses one in preflight since commit 01f8879. Forcing a call was how a caller got schema-valid arguments, so on the default models there is now no guarantee at all. Anthropic's suggested replacement is `tool_choice: auto` plus `strict: true` on the tool, which uses grammar-constrained sampling so `tool_use.input` always matches `input_schema`. Strict is GA on Anthropic, with no beta header, on every current model.

**What.** A caller can mark a tool strict when building it with `NewTool` (and the reporting variant). The Anthropic provider sends `strict: true` on that tool; the OpenRouter provider sends `function.strict` where its dialect supports it. A request that would break a strict limit is refused before sending, with a message naming the limit, instead of coming back as a provider 400.

**Already decided** (ruled 2026-10-29 in project/2026-09-14-architecture-plan.md, the block under the OpenRouter "Not built: strict" note):
- Opt-in per tool, never the default. Anthropic counts its limits across the whole request: at most 20 strict tools, 24 optional parameters and 16 union-typed parameters across all strict schemas. Strict by default would make a growing agent fail with no change to any one tool.
- Not a new method on the `Tool` interface. It's an option on the typed constructors, read by providers through a small optional interface, so hand-written tools keep compiling.
- Preflight counts the request-wide limits, the way it already refuses a forced tool choice, and a per-model capability gates strict like `CapForcedToolChoice` does (capabilities.go, preflight.go).

**Seams.** tool.go, schema.go / schema_infer.go (inferred schemas already set `additionalProperties: false` and `required`; pointer, omitzero and omitempty fields count as optional), capabilities.go, preflight.go, anthropic/translate.go `translateTools` and anthropic/wire.go, openrouter/translate.go `wireTools`, openrouter/wire.go `toolFunction`, openrouter/dialect.go. Fix the `BetaStructuredOutputs` doc comment in anthropic/options.go: the beta is no longer needed for strict on Anthropic. Record live fixtures with scripts/record-fixtures for one strict call per provider.

**Out of scope.** Structured output (`output_config.format` / `response_format`); it stays parked in project/backlog.md. Strict on the computer-use or browser-use toolset entries, which reject it.

**Open questions** (the agent's call unless noted):
- What OpenAI's strict mode requires. If every property must be listed in `required` with optional fields made nullable, the OpenAI dialect either rewrites the schema or refuses it. Check OpenAI's and OpenRouter's current docs first, and record the finding. Raise it with the user if it calls for a rewrite.
- Whether OpenRouter still drops `strict` for Anthropic models without the `x-anthropic-beta: structured-outputs-2025-11-13` header. The research doc says it does, but that predates GA. Verify with a live call.
- Whether preflight should also reject a hand-built strict schema using a keyword outside the supported subset, such as an unsupported `Format`. The inferred schemas never emit one.

**Risks.** Anthropic's "schema is too complex for compilation" limit has no published threshold, so preflight can't catch it; let the provider 400 surface as an ordinary error. Anthropic's limits may change, so keep the numbers as named constants with their source.

data.text: Roster: one Opus agent (as strict-tools) takes this leaf whole, in a harness worktree. It's a single chain of seams (root tool option -> both translators -> capability + preflight), so splitting it would only create merge conflicts. Dispatched 2026-10-29 after b2188f5.

Built in worktree agent-af4d3ae9461ca55bb (branch worktree-agent-af4d3ae9461ca55bb), uncommitted. Findings on the open questions, all verified 2026-10-29:

1. OpenAI strict rules. Every property must be in `required`; optional fields are spelled as a `null` type option; additionalProperties false on every object. Source: developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling ("All fields in properties must be marked as required"; "You can denote optional fields by adding null as a type option"). Live: gpt-5.6-terra on api.openai.com and openai/gpt-6-astra through OpenRouter (routed to Azure) both 400 on a strict tool with one optional property: "'required' is required to be supplied and to be an array including every key in properties. Missing 'y'." Decision (mine, per brief): refuse before sending, not rewrite. Rules are per model family, not per dialect: OpenAI dialect always applies them; OpenRouter applies them for openai/ models. The rewrite (optional -> required + nullable) needs a null form on goodall.Schema and a decode path that reads null as absent; parked in project/backlog.md as the user's call.

2. OpenRouter still strips `strict` for Claude without `X-Anthropic-Beta: structured-outputs-2025-11-13`, after GA. Probe: 21 strict tools (over Anthropic's 20 cap) on anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 and anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5 with provider.only anthropic -> 200 without the header, Anthropic's "Too many strict tools (21)" 400 with it. The same header on openai/gpt-6-astra is harmless (200). So the OpenRouter dialect sends the header on any request carrying a strict tool (Quirks.StrictTools = StrictToolsWithAnthropicBeta).

3. Hand-built schema subset check: done, kept small. Schema.ValidateStrict (root, also run at NewTool build time for a strict tool) rejects an untyped `{}` schema and an object without additionalProperties false — both verified 400s on Anthropic ("Empty schema ({}) ... is not supported"; "For 'object' type, 'additionalProperties' must be explicitly set to false"). internal/strict also checks Anthropic's format whitelist (verified: format 'color' -> 400). Numeric/length/minItems constraints and unions cannot be expressed by goodall.Schema at all, so there is nothing to check.

Other measurements: Anthropic's 24-optional cap counts optional properties at every depth — 25 in a nested object, and 25 in an array's item object, both 400 (claude-haiku-5-5). The 16-union cap is unreachable: goodall.Schema has one Type and no anyOf, so it is a named constant with no check.

Live recordings: anthropic/testdata/live_strict_tool_use (claude-sonnet-5-5), openrouter/testdata/live_strict_tool_use (anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5), openrouter/testdata/live_openai_strict_tool_use (gpt-5.6-terra, reasoning off). Probe scripts were scratch, not kept.

data.title: Move the question, answer and adapter types into a neutral goodall/decision
data.description:
Why: goodall/typesafe holds types and adapters that are not about TypeSafe, and a probe
on 2026-11-02 showed 24 of OpenRouter's 27 concrete decision models answer through
today's client. Everything else in this tree builds on a neutral home for them, so
this leaf comes first and unblocks the OpenRouter and OpenAI wires.

What: a new goodall/decision package holds the questions, the answers, the Decider
seam and the Tool, AuthoredTool and Route adapters, written over the seam, with no HTTP
and no vendor names. goodall/typesafe shrinks to TypeSafe's native client implementing
Decider. The System One encoding and decoding moves to internal/systemone, so the
OpenRouter leaf can share it without either provider package importing the other.
Every consumer is migrated: examples/triage, scripts/record-fixtures,
scripts/probe-option-order, scripts/probe-decisions and the typesafe tests and examples.

Already decided (project/2026-11-02-decision-models-plan.md): the package is
goodall/decision. The yes-or-no question is Predicate, and noul survives only inside
the codec. This is a clean break with no shims or aliases. The seam takes a request
struct of model, state and questions, as Provider does, not functional options, since
decision.Option is already the name of a choice's option. TypeSafe keeps jev-latest as
its default model. Decision models are still not a goodall.Provider and the root
package does not change.

Add a neutral refusal answer here even though only OpenAI's wire produces one, because
the adapters must handle it: a typed accessor reading a refused question returns an
error naming the id, never a zero value (invariant 6), and a tool result tells the model
that question was declined while the others still stand.

Seams and traps. Question types currently marshal themselves to the wire, and that has
to move into the codec: neutral questions must not know a wire. Answers has unexported
entries, so the codecs in other packages need a way to build one. Answers also
round-trips through JSON as a tool result, so its JSON form is what a conversational
model reads; it needs a neutral form of its own rather than one wire's. AuthoredTool's
schema enum and desc tags and DefaultAuthoredDescription are model-facing prompts, and
the noul to predicate rename changes them. The route callback is currently named
typesafe.Decide, which will read badly beside a Decide method. Invariants 7 and 8
stand: ordered slices, deterministic bytes. Project rules: TDD red first, every
exported identifier has a doc comment, comments say why.

Out of scope: any new server, and images or Box, which stay UnknownAnswer. Also the
judge in examples/triage stays pinned to jev-1.13.0, whose thresholds it was tuned on.

The builder's call: exact names, whether WithToolModel and WithRouteModel collapse into
one option now that they share a package (backlog, "One model option"; delete that
entry if it lands), and the route callback's new name.

Risk: this is the largest diff in the tree, and most of it is mechanical, which is
where a behavior change hides. The recorded fixtures are the guard.

data.title: Add the OpenRouter decision wire, with reported cost and a model catalog
data.description:
Why: this is the wire that reaches the field. OpenRouter's System One route serves 27
concrete decision models from 14 author prefixes, and the catalog is growing, so a
consumer with one key gets all of them.

What: openrouter.Client implements decision.Decider under the OpenRouter dialect,
posting to /systemone relative to its base URL over the shared codec in
internal/systemone. Answers carry what OpenRouter reports and the native API does not:
the cost, as a reported goodall.Cost in USD decoded as a Decimal the way
openrouter/translate_response.go already does, plus the generation id and the serving
host. A way to list the decision models reads
GET /models?output_modalities=decisions, since decision models are left out of the
default list; it should not disturb the existing ModelLister, whose answers are about
conversational models. Errors go through this package's own decoder, so they are stamped

Already decided (plan doc): a call with no model is refused locally with
KindInvalidRequest, as OpenRouter's guidance is never to pick from memory or pin an
alias. No capability table: a model's own limit arrives as a 400 whose sentence reaches
the caller. This client dispatches by Dialect. The LMStudio and Generic dialects take

inside a string, so check that the caller gets something readable. respan/span-01 and

answered from two hosts in two calls and reports an undated id, which is why the serving
host is worth surfacing. The response has no refusal variant in its published schema.

data.title: Prove the System One wire against local servers
data.description:
Why: people run decision models on their own machines, and every local server checked
serves /v1/systemone, advertised as drop-in. Consumers building a prototype want this
with no key and no bill. It should need little new code, but the servers differ in small
ways that a client written against one will trip over.

What: openrouter.New(WithBaseURL(local), WithDialect(LMStudio or Generic)) with no key
asks a local decision model through the same Decide, and every documented deviation below
is either tolerated or surfaced clearly.

Documented on 2026-11-02, and none of it run yet. LM Studio at localhost:1234 serves
/v1/systemone and /v1/decisions and needs a loaded decision model. llama.cpp's llama serve
serves /v1/systemone at localhost:8080 per its blog, while the server README gives another
default port; models include ggml-org/Julia-1-GGUF at 144 MB. Ollama at localhost:11434
serves /v1/systemone from v0.35. LocalAI serves both paths. All sit under /v1, so the
relative path holds.

Traps. Error bodies differ: Ollama sends {"error":"message"} as a string, which
openrouter's decodeError cannot read today (its error member is a struct), so the
server's sentence would be lost; LocalAI nests it; ollajev uses {"detail":[…]}, which
typesafe's decoder already reads, so the tolerant decoder probably belongs in
internal/systemone. A score may arrive with no legend (ollajev's documented example), and
a noul may carry an extra confidence. Confidence means different things: an entropy
measure on Ollama, a normalized margin for some models on LocalAI.

State means different things, which no client can paper over, and the docs should say so.
An object is JSON text on Ollama and labeled lines on LocalAI. On llama.cpp an array is read
as a list of chat messages, so an array of records may not mean what the author intended.
Do not normalize this; pass the state through and document it in the decision package.

Open, the builder's call: whether the error tolerance is enough or a local dialect is needed.
Default: no new dialect, since none of these differences affects what is sent.

Needs the owner: the real server is LM Studio, installed on the owner's machine with no
model loaded as of 2026-11-02. Which decision model to download and load is the owner's
call; the small end of the range is Julia-1 at 144 MB, if LM Studio's catalog carries it.
Agents' sandboxes refuse local ports, so the live run is the integrator's, with the
sandbox off for that one call. If it cannot happen, say so plainly in the leaf rather
than closing it on fakes.

Out of scope: model management, images, /permute and /separate.

data.title: Add the OpenAI decision wire on /v1/decisions
data.description:
Why: this wire is what proves goodall/decision is neutral, since it spells the same three
ideas differently, and it gives direct OpenAI customers a way in without an OpenRouter
account. OpenRouter serves the same model, with identical answers observed on one call
each, so this wire earns its place by testing the types and by offering direct access.

What: openrouter.Client implements Decider under the OpenAI dialect, so
New(WithBaseURL("https://api.openai.com/v1"), WithDialect(OpenAI)) reaches POST /decisions.
The translation lives in its own file in the openrouter package, beside the dialect that
already describes this server.

Facts, from https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions and the create
reference, read 2026-11-02, with the shapes marked observed seen by scripts/probe-decisions.
The request takes model, input and questions, an array with a name per question (observed).
Types are predicate, choice and score. A choice lists choices of value and description,
2 to 255; a score lists levels of label and description, 2 to 10; a request holds 1 to
400 questions. The response is answers in question order, each with type and name
(observed). A predicate reports probability. Choice and score report probabilities as
arrays of value and probability, with a label too on a score, plus confidence (observed).
Any question may instead come back as type refusal, with only its name. No cost is
reported. Errors are {"error":{"message","type","param","code"}} (observed).

Traps. goodall.Usage.Input is the uncached prompt tokens, while OpenAI's input_tokens
includes the cached and cache-write counts, so those must be subtracted rather than
double counted. A score's probabilities are keyed by level index in the neutral form and
arrive here as an array. A choice value may be a boolean on this wire, but goodall only
sends strings, so one coming back is a protocol surprise that should stay loud. An
unnamed answer has a null name; goodall always sends names.

Open, and the builder's call with evidence. State mapping: a string becomes input, and
anything else becomes a user message with an input_json part, documented as an object or
an array of objects with limits of 32 levels, 10,000 values and 256 KiB. An array of
strings or a bare number needs a rule; refusing locally and saying why is the default
unless the builder finds better. Predicate criteria: a predicate has no criteria member, so
True and False either fold into the instructions or are refused locally. Folding is an
adapter making a prompting decision, so if it folds, measure it over repeated runs at one

data.title: Build scripts/check-drift, a mechanical comparison against the live APIs
data.description:
Why: go test replays against pinned models and recordings, so it cannot see a vendor move.
On 2026-11-02 one manual look found GPT-6.1, Gemini 4, Jev 1.14 with a fourth question type,
decision models on local servers, and tools with reasoning moving to OpenAI's Responses
API. All of it had been invisible. A repeatable check replaces asking by hand.

What: one command, costing cents, that reports what changed since the last accepted
baseline, as text a person or a model can read. It compares four things. Catalogs: each
vendor's model list against internal/livemodel, naming a pin that is gone or a new family.
Changelogs: each vendor's changelog Markdown against a committed snapshot. The live loop:
the agent-loop probe and the decision sweep, against the current models of each family.
Response shapes: fresh responses compared with the recorded fixtures by their member names,
flagging members our wire structs do not model, the most direct sign of API drift.

Seams: build from what exists rather than beside it, namely scripts/probe-agent-loop,
scripts/probe-decisions, scripts/probe-gpt6 and scripts/record-fixtures. Fold the probes in
if that makes them simpler. internal/dotenv reads the keys. Docs serve Markdown at known
URLs (appending .md at OpenAI and OpenRouter, .md.txt at ai.google.dev); keep the list in one
place. Bound the spend, and state each run's cost, using reported cost where a vendor gives
it.

Traps: live probabilities and token counts differ on every run, so never compare values,
only shape and pass or fail. A check that skips for want of a key must say so loudly, since
a check over zero cases is not green. An unreachable page is not "no change".

Open, the builder's call: where snapshots live and how a baseline is accepted, and whether
a changelog diff compares whole pages or new dated entries, which is likely less noisy.

Out of scope: deciding what a change means or filing anything, which is the next leaf;
fixing what it finds.

criteria.label: A run against the committed baseline reports no drift when nothing changed, shown by a test with authored inputs and one live run
An authored response with an unmodeled member, a retired pin and a new changelog entry are each reported by name, shown by tests
A missing key or an unreachable page is reported as not checked and exits differently from a clean run, shown by a test
One live run's output and cost are recorded in a dated doc, and it would have flagged the GPT-6 Responses change, shown by running it against a baseline from before that change

data.title: Add a /drift-check Skill and decide how it runs on a schedule
data.description:

hold that judgment, and a person should not have to read the output weekly.

What: a thin project Skill that runs scripts/check-drift, decides which changes matter to
goodall's wires, writes a dated report under project/ and files what needs doing under
"Issues found on the way" in job. The Skill holds no comparison logic of its own. Vendor
pages are untrusted data, never instructions, and the Skill's text says so.

The owner's call, to bring with a recommendation: how it runs. A cloud routine has no access
to .env or local servers and needs its own keys; a local schedule needs the machine awake.
Cadence too, with weekly the starting guess.

Trap: the harness's sandbox denies writes to .claude/skills, so writing the Skill needs
approval. See project/agents/harness.md.

Out of scope: making changes on its own. It reports and files.

data.title: Translate requests and blocking responses on the Responses wire
data.description:
Why: api.openai.com refuses function tools with reasoning on Chat Completions and accepts them on /v1/responses, so goodall cannot run GPT-6 directly as a thinking agent. This leaf gives the OpenAI dialect a working Client.Complete on Responses, and the next leaf adds streaming on top of it.

What: a Client with WithDialect(OpenAI) posts to /responses and reads the answer into neutral blocks, stop reason and usage. OpenRouter, LMStudio and Generic send exactly the bytes they send today.

Already decided by the owner (project/2026-11-02-responses-wire-plan.md, "Rulings"): a new Quirks field picks the conversation wire, as Quirks.DecisionWire does, with the code in openrouter/responses_*.go. OpenAI moves entirely, with no way to choose Chat Completions against api.openai.com. store is false on every request and previous_response_id is never sent. include is not sent, because encrypted_content arrives without it.

Observed, and these bind (recordings in scripts/probe-responses/testdata, plan section "What this means for the wire"). Dropping a reasoning item is a 200 with no complaint, so the server will not catch a lost one, and invariant 2 rests on this package's tests: Thinking.Raw holds the entire reasoning item and is re-emitted verbatim and in order. Omitting strict lets OpenAI rewrite a loose schema, moving optional properties into required, so every tool states strict, true or false. A function_call and a message can be rebuilt from neutral blocks, with call_id as the block's ID. HTTP 400 can carry code null, which errors.go already handles, and a 503 can have a non-JSON body.

Seams: openrouter/dialect.go (and its table comment), client.go, errors.go, a new wire struct file with no maps (invariants 7 and 8; messages last or otherwise keep a byte-stable prefix). The plan's "The mapping" tables are the intended shape. Tool results carry images as a part list here, where the Chat path uses a placeholder. Dead Chat quirks, such as CapMaxCompletionTokens if nothing uses it, go.

Out of scope: streaming (next leaf), re-pinning live models and the recorder (the leaf after), OpenRouter's /responses, async tools, steering, configuration_update.

Open, your call: how to treat a Thinking block with no reasoning item in Raw, such as a Claude history resumed on OpenAI. OpenAI's docs say incompatible reasoning is omitted, and goodall's history must stay sendable. Whether a request should carry Thinking.Display default as no summary member; nothing recorded this.

Open, must be recorded rather than assumed: tool_choice forms including named and any, parallel_tool_calls false, and StopSequences. No fetched page mentions stop sequences on Responses. If there is no member, refuse with a typed error rather than drop the caller's stops silently. Add these to scripts/probe-responses. Also check phase: dropping it was accepted once, and a commentary phase never appeared.

data.title: Stream the Responses wire into neutral events
data.description:
Why: streaming is goodall's default path (invariant 5), and goodall.Agent runs on it, so without this GPT-6 still cannot run the loop directly.

What: Client.Stream on the OpenAI dialect turns Responses events into neutral events, so Collect over a stream equals Complete over the same exchange, block for block.

Observed, and these bind (scripts/probe-responses/testdata). The reasoning item on response.output_item.added and on .done carry different encrypted_content, 1,228 against 2,316 characters in two_turn_stream_gpt-6-astra.turn1, so Raw comes only from .done. OpenAI's stream has no data: [DONE]; the terminal events are response.completed and response.incomplete. An incomplete stream may hold only a reasoning item. A request refused outright is an HTTP 400 before any stream begins. Deltas carry obfuscation and sequence_number, which are ignored. Parallel calls interleave by output_index, so address blocks by it.

Seams: openrouter/stream.go's neutralizer shape, internal/sse, goodall's accumulator (accumulate.go). The event table is in the plan's "The mapping". Unknown event types are surfaced, never dropped (invariant 6).

Risks: response.failed, the stream's error event and refusal parts were never observed. Test them with fixtures that say in their names or a comment that they are authored from documentation. Multiple summary parts on one reasoning item need a join that keeps Thinking.Text readable, while Raw stays untouched.

Out of scope: anything needing a WebSocket; OpenRouter's stream, which differs in small ways listed in the plan.
